answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 38 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the ledge hash is checked against the pigment checkpoint at intake, the haven audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 4764 identities would post 683 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
